findings.where: case.statement and notes ('F16, F17, F44'); case.statement ('adopting Vinge's discontinuity criterion over the growth criterion')
findings.finding: The case reading agrees (see case_agrees), but one cited support does not bear. F16 records disagreement about when or whether human intelligence will be surpassed. It is not evidence that the field holds the term as plural. The field's real marginal holding of a non-superintelligence sense is F17 (broader use), together with F44/F49 (Britannica's technology-synthesis definition). Separately, 'over the growth criterion' raises the B.2 locus, which says 'more directly than'.
findings.evidence: F16: "Technology forecasters and researchers disagree about when, or whether, human intelligence will be surpassed."; #1637 B.2: "The contingent-singularity model adopts the discontinuity criterion more directly than the growth criterion"
findings.fix: Replace '(F16, F17, F44)' with '(F17, F44, F49)' in case.statement and notes. Replace 'adopting Vinge's discontinuity criterion over the growth criterion' with 'adopting the discontinuity criterion more directly than the growth criterion'.

summary: The case reading holds. Equal, ρ = extends is supported by verbatim loci (#1637 B.6 'a distinct member of the family, not a correction to every existing one', §31 coexistence, §2.5, §37; #1635 Abstract and §1), and the field's own broader sense (F17) and synthesis definition (F44/F49) show the field holds a non-superintelligence sense, so the witness law does not apply. A reader of the same papers would decide the same, though F16 should drop out of the support. The KO's sentences are entailed by their ledger quotes, attributed, and verbatim in the texts, and the translation table is complete and verbatim. The defects are in the compression: a kernel claim (F30) cut, with the cut log wrongly saying no kernel claim was cut; archive and field claims left unattributed; and several force shifts (Dates, Re-objected, Thorstad 'misses it'). In the KO: two force fixes (KO 12, 28), a dropped clause (KO 4) and a lede ordering question (KO 1). The ledger lacks #1635/#1637 §0's 'no fixed sign' statement, so open item 2 asks for a statement the paper already makes.
